citations.narrative:
A primary enclosure housing four ring-tailed lemurs is not being maintained so that it protects the nonhuman primates
from injury. Within the lemur primary enclosure is a wooden shelter located above a dirt floor. Beneath this shelter is a
hole in the ground where dirt has been dug out. Several big pieces of rock that are irregular in size reside within it. The
hole extends outward to the right of the shelter leaving the shelter inclined to the right and into this hole.
The ring-tailed lemur shelter is placed above unsecure ground leaving the animals at risk of harm. Failure to maintain a
properly constructed primary enclosure floor may result in the shelter falling onto and injuring the animals. Primary
enclosures must be constructed and maintained so that they have floors that are constructed in a manner that protects
the nonhuman primates from injuring themselves.
Correct by 9/7/26

The housing facility for an adult male giraffe is in need of repair. A fixed knot fence surrounds the giraffe's primary
enclosure. To the right side of the enclosure, the fence is no longer securely attached onto the metal fence posts. These
metal posts have inclined away from the enclosure causing the fence to detach. As a result, approximately two thirds the
length of the top of the fence has bent over into the enclosure.
The wire fence is no longer strong enough to contain the giraffe and places the animal at risk of injury. The facility must be
constructed of material that is appropriate in strength for the animals involved. The indoor and outdoor housing facilities
shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to contain them.
Correct by 10/11/26
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
